This catalogue is a planning baseline. Its test specifications remain not run; actual development observations are recorded separately in work records and candidate-bound evidence. The original roadmap, ADR-0042 additions and ADR-0044 browser additions retain separate source provenance. Source-system qualification, human decisions and actual pilot observations cannot be replaced with simulated success.

Start with M00-G01. Give each worker one packet after its dependencies are accepted. Use the installed git-agent workflow, ordinary project commands and one writer per isolated worktree. Every accepted feature adds protected regression obligations.

Complete Markdown catalogue · Machine-readable goals · Worker contract · Regression strategy · Evidence contract

Browser roadmap added October 19, 2026. Read the M23–M25 worker handoff for current M14 progress and the recommended browser batch. The initial M00 dispatch text remains a historical baseline, not a reset of completed work.

M00 — Product charter and reproducible development

Establish a buildable project and an accepted product boundary before implementation becomes a collection of unrelated agent experiments.

M00-G01 · Freeze the first-release support envelope
governancenormal riskhuman_decisionnot started

Outcome: Create versioned charter and capability/support-envelope records naming first customer, Shopify-first/WooCommerce-second scope, actions, payment/fulfillment exclusions and release claims; obtain human approval.

Depends on: No prior goal; obtain the actual charter decision.

Owned scope: charter/ADRs/support-envelope; planning schemas and validation fixtures. Proposed modules; bind to real repository paths.

Required tests and independent oracles

CASE-M00-G01-01 · positive

Arrange / act: Validate a named supported order-status and return scenario against the approved matrix

Assert: Every scenario resolves to a supported, conditional or explicitly excluded capability with a reason and accountable owner.

CASE-M00-G01-02 · negative

Arrange / act: Introduce a refund/payment combination absent from the envelope

Assert: Validation rejects an automatic supported label and requires a reviewed scope decision.

CASE-M00-G01-03 · regression

Arrange / act: Remove an already accepted capability from the matrix

Assert: Baseline comparison detects the removal and blocks an unchanged release claim.

Broken behavior to detect: Delete one accepted capability row while keeping its advertised release claim.

Evidence and acceptance

  • manifest.json: candidate/base SHA, source-tree/build digests, config/skill/policy/model/adapter pins, environment, fixture hashes and actual timestamps.
  • tests/native-report.* and tests/results.json: exact commands/exit codes, discovered and executed stable case IDs, totals and native report hashes; zero-test/skip/todo is not pass.
  • red-green.md: observed behavioral red failure or valid targeted mutant failure, repaired-candidate pass, and the exact code/config change that caused each outcome.
  • demo.md plus sanitized API trace or UI recording: demonstrate the named outcome on this candidate; screenshots alone do not establish money or stock correctness.
  • regression-review.md: compare accepted capability/test baseline, changed/deleted tests and oracle files, compatibility, migrations and old journeys; independent reviewer decision.
  • security-review.md: independent authority/tenant/secret/side-effect review proportional to risk; no self-approval for critical changes.
  • handoff.md: implementation paths, actual commands, remaining limits, rollback/recovery, deployment/support implications and next unblocked goals.
  • decision.json: trusted integration owner/maintainer acceptance is separate from author evidence; public/tagged release requires human authorization.
  • Human-approved charter; capability matrix; decision record; checks over supported and excluded fixtures.

Preserve: Run own tests plus all accepted tests impacted by this change, all introduced cross-cutting invariants, and the deterministic regression suite. Milestone/release candidate runs the full applicable accepted suite and required connected qualification.

M01-G01 · Implement tenant-scoped canonical resources
identitycritical risklocalnot started

Outcome: Persist tenant/store/source-system/external-ID/version keys and apply scoped reads to database queries, APIs, jobs and attachment references. Add minimal operator identity for the read-only slice.

Assert: The boundary rejects the operation before querying shared data.

Original milestone exit criteria

  • Human takeover stops further agent actions without losing case context; new messages in other channels do not bypass customer verification.
  • Verified policy answers and completed business actions are measured separately from attempts; all sampled financial outcomes reconcile.
  • Provider outage or budget exhaustion falls back to queued/manual operation; no new provider receives customer data without merchant approval.
  • Opt-out arriving concurrently with a scheduled marketing message suppresses the send; transactional behavior follows configured consent/policy rules.

M15 — Sender-bound remote agent access

Add one standards-based remote authorization profile to the existing task and worker boundaries, so possession of a copied token alone cannot read case data or prepare a proposal. Keep tenant, customer, task, policy, approval, lease and stop decisions in the existing server authority.

M15-G01 · Define one remote trust profile over current task authority
securitycritical risklocal_then_separate_qualificationnot started

Outcome: Specify a remote identity and sender-binding contract whose only authority comes from verified issuer claims and existing server-side task permissions.

Depends on: M02-G18, M02-G19, M02-G99, M07-G99

Owned scope: Define a narrow RemoteTaskAuthenticator result containing trusted issuer and audience, original principal and current actor, sender-key thumbprint, token expiry, task ceiling and an internal server-resolved task scope.; Configure an exact issuer, allowed signing algorithms and key sources, resource audience, canonical HTTPS origin, accepted confirmation mechanism and bounded clock/replay windows. Do not select issuer, key URL or audience from arbitrary client input.; Map the authenticated principal to current tenant, store, customer/case and permitted operations using existing server state. Treat caller-supplied identifiers as requested resources, not evidence of membership.; Select the RFC 9449 DPoP resource-server profile and an existing supported issuer/library integration. If the selected issuer cannot issue or confirm sender-bound tokens, leave that remote profile unavailable.; Keep the current loopback-only opaque read grant and local worker contract explicit. A configured remote profile must never reinterpret a local grant as OAuth.. Proposed modules; bind to real repository paths.

M15-G02 · Verify sender proof at the actual remote resource boundary
securitycritical risklocal_then_separate_qualificationnot started

Outcome: Require a valid sender-bound token and a fresh proof on each supported remote request, with no bearer downgrade.

Depends on: M15-G01, M02-G99, M07-G99

Owned scope: Use the selected library for issuer-token verification and cryptographic proof verification. Enforce trusted token confirmation, asymmetric proof algorithm, dpop+jwt type and the public proof key's thumbprint match.; Validate the RFC 9449 method and target-URI binding, access-token hash, proof time and nonce when the selected profile requires it. Derive the effective URL from configured origin/proxy trust; ignore untrusted forwarded-host rewrites.; Keep token audience verification distinct from proof target verification. RFC 9449 htu excludes query and fragment; existing gateway and resource validation must independently validate query parameters and request bodies.; Place verification on the origin route, including direct access that bypasses an optional portal. Do not treat a user-agent header, portal visibility or possession of the token as sender authentication.; Keep proof keys outside model prompts, skill files and model-generated code in the provided client. M15-G03 · Fence replay, revocation and active work across verifier processes
securitycritical risklocal_then_separate_qualificationnot started

Outcome: Make proof replay and current task restrictions effective across concurrent requests, restarts and lease renewal.

Depends on: M15-G02, M02-G20, M02-G21, M02-G99, M07-G99

Owned scope: Add bounded shared replay admission with an atomic uniqueness decision for the appropriate issuer/sender/proof identifier, retaining entries through the accepted proof window and skew allowance.; Fail closed when replay admission or required current-authority reads are unavailable. Do not fall back to an instance-local Map or silently clear the active replay window on restart.; Reuse current parent-session, membership, policy, configuration, stop and lease-generation checks. Token lifetime, lease renewal and client handoff cannot exceed the original task ceiling or recover revoked scope.; Record minimized denial/admission reasons and references to the current actor, original principal and task. Never persist raw access tokens, proof JWTs or private keys in receipts.; Preserve existing unknown-operation reconciliation semantics: retrying authentication or taking over a lease must not create a fresh identity for an already attempted business effect.. Proposed modules; bind to real repository paths.

Required tests and independent oracles

CASE-M15-G03-01 · positive

Arrange / act: Exercise the declared scenario with authorized synthetic data and the required independent source evidence. Run a bounded two-process replay race, revoke the task while one client holds a valid token, and show the next read/renewal denied while a pre-existing unknown operation remains available to authorized reconciliation.

Assert: Two verifier processes race the same valid proof against the shared store: at most one request is admitted. A restart within the proof window does not make the proof reusable.

CASE-M15-G03-02 · negative

Arrange / act: Exercise the declared scenario with authorized synthetic data and the required independent source evidence. Run a bounded two-process replay race, revoke the task while one client holds a valid token, and show the next read/renewal denied while a pre-existing unknown operation remains available to authorized reconciliation.

Assert: Revoked membership/session, an expired task, a stop revision and a stale lease generation deny the relevant next operation or renewal even when the token and cryptographic proof are valid.

CASE-M15-G03-03 · regression

Arrange / act: Apply the named targeted fault to the declared scenario. Run a bounded two-process replay race, revoke the task while one client holds a valid token, and show the next read/renewal denied while a pre-existing unknown operation remains available to authorized reconciliation.

Assert: Replay-store failure denies protected access and records a bounded reason; recovery restores service without accepting retained replays or reopening expired tasks.

Broken behavior to detect: Replace atomic replay admission with a process-local check, or omit the current stop/lease fence; a two-process race or revoked-work fixture must detect the regression.

Arrange / act: Exercise the declared scenario with authorized synthetic data and the required independent source evidence. Assert: An ambiguous synthetic effect followed by an authenticated takeover remains attached to its original operation identity and proceeds through reconciliation without a second send.

  • No source baseline, accepted-goal ledger or unsupported external-host guarantee is changed by this research proposal.

M16 — Managed execution security

Qualify one operator-managed runner boundary with mediated network access, constrained resources and a bounded two-branch restriction demonstration, while stating the narrower guarantees available for external agents. Keep AI Gateway use optional.

M16-G01 · Define managed coverage and the typed broker boundary
securitycritical risklocal_then_separate_qualificationnot started

Outcome: Identify exactly which task inputs, outputs and runtime resources Rifare controls, and mediate them through the existing server authority.

Depends on: M15-G01, M02-G10, M02-G19, M15-G99

Owned scope: Define one managed runner profile and a narrow broker protocol for permitted evidence reads, model requests, proposals and typed outputs. Keep tenant and effective authority server-resolved on every request.; Reuse existing action schemas, exact-preview approvals, model-route bounds, credential handles, receipts, stops and reconciliation. The broker is a mediation boundary, not a second business policy engine.; Permit only configured operation/destination combinations; do not expose a generic URL fetcher, arbitrary CONNECT tunnel, raw database connection or direct commerce adapter to the runner.; Describe managed process, trusted broker and external-agent coverage separately. External task contexts are minimized and labeled with applicable handling obligations; API checks cannot prove external deletion or egress control.; Treat input provenance and effective authority as memory/cache partition keys. A saved context cannot silently cross tenant/task or carry broader permissions into a restricted continuation.. Proposed modules; bind to real repository paths.

M16-G02 · Enforce one real isolation and egress profile
securitycritical risklocal_then_separate_qualificationnot started

Outcome: Run the supported managed agent in a constrained environment that cannot bypass the broker to reach the network, host secrets or sibling tasks.

Place the broker and provider/commerce credentials outside runner reach.; Constrain filesystem mounts, per-task scratch, process namespace and privileges; prevent access to host sockets, metadata endpoints and sibling-task state. M16-G03 · Persist narrower authority before admitting protected data
securitycritical risklocal_then_separate_qualificationnot started

Missing acknowledgements, version conflicts and unavailable state fail closed.; For in-flight work, drain, cancel or reauthorize the affected channels according to the supported transport. Original milestone exit criteria

  • The selected real managed-runner profile denies broker bypass and demonstrates the declared resource/secret boundary with candidate-bound local evidence.
  • The fixed two-branch protected-data workflow fences the removed route before admission, survives the tested restart/failure cases and preserves the named useful operations.
  • Managed and external-agent coverage is explicit; the result is not generalized to uncontrolled hosts, arbitrary graphs or already completed external effects.

ADD-M19-G03 · Reserve and reconcile loyalty redemption

M21-G05 · Prepare supplies replenishment and gate recurring purchases
warehouse_intelligencecritical risklocal_then_separate_qualificationnot started

Outcome: Default to threshold/scheduled PO drafts that account for stock and open orders; optionally execute recurring purchases only through a separately activated, bounded merchant mandate and qualified supplier.

Depends on: M21-G04, M11-G04, M11-G05, M11-G06, M11-G07, M08-G99, M11-G99

Owned scope: Versioned threshold and schedule configuration; One logical replenishment request or mandate occurrence per trigger; Existing PO, budget, approval and original-identity reconciliation integration; Optional mandate contract for exact merchant, supplier account, allowed SKUs, quantity limits, currency, per-order and aggregate spend caps, validity and revocation; Version-bound mandate approval by a principal with M11-G06 procurement authority, with the existing separation of duties. Proposed modules; bind to real repository paths.

Required tests and independent oracles

CASE-M21-G05-01 · positive

Arrange / act: Exercise the declared scenario with authorized synthetic data and the required independent source evidence. Start with a low-stock observation that creates only a draft. If the optional capability is qualified, activate a bounded test mandate, lose one supplier acknowledgment, reconcile the original occurrence, then revoke the mandate before the next dispatch.

Assert: Without an explicitly active mandate capability, a threshold or schedule creates only one explainable PO draft. Repeated observations, open POs and partial receipts cannot duplicate the same uncovered need or authorize a supplier call.

CASE-M21-G05-02 · negative

Arrange / act: Exercise the declared scenario with authorized synthetic data and the required independent source evidence. Start with a low-stock observation that creates only a draft. If the optional capability is qualified, activate a bounded test mandate, lose one supplier acknowledgment, reconcile the original occurrence, then revoke the mandate before the next dispatch.

Assert: When the optional path is separately qualified, a principal with M11-G06 procurement approval authority approves its versioned mandate terms, preserving required separation of duties. The proposing or executing agent cannot activate or widen it. Each occurrence rechecks current mandate and authorizing authority, fixed merchant/supplier/SKU terms, stock and open-PO evidence, exact purchase preview, approved quantities and atomic per-order/aggregate spend reservations. Covered changes require new approval.

CASE-M21-G05-03 · regression

Arrange / act: Apply the named targeted fault to the declared scenario. Start with a low-stock observation that creates only a draft. If the optional capability is qualified, activate a bounded test mandate, lose one supplier acknowledgment, reconcile the original occurrence, then revoke the mandate before the next dispatch.

Assert: A timeout after supplier acceptance keeps the original mandate occurrence and purchase identity unknown. Its unresolved stock/order commitment and applicable mandate/budget reservations persist across timeout, restart, mandate expiry and later triggers until authoritative reconciliation or cancellation resolves the outcome. Retries reconcile the original identity; another occurrence cannot consume the same committed need or reserved capacity.

Broken behavior to detect: Let a drafting agent activate its own recurring mandate, retry an unknown purchase under a new request key, or release its reserved budget so a later occurrence can spend the same capacity.

Assert: Revocation, expiry, changed supplier or price outside approved bounds before dispatch blocks the recurring effect and preserves a draft/exception. The evidence states whether only drafts or actual qualified mandate execution was observed.
